title: MISSION 01 — THE NEMEAN LION
subtitle: THE LION’S GRIP
paragraphs: The Nemean Lion was a monstrous beast whose skin could not be pierced by ordinary weapons. Hercules defeated it using his own strength, completing his first legendary labor.

Mighty Maximilian, welcome to your first trial. Unfortunately, the lion has absolutely no intention of cooperating. And Phil says those marathon legs won’t save you this time. You’ll need some serious grip strength.
1 Goggins — 2 rounds: 20 sec hang, 10 rows, 40 sec carry
2 Goggins — 3 rounds: 30 sec hang, 12 rows, 60 sec carry
3 Goggins — 4 rounds: 30–40 sec hang, 10–12 slow eccentric rows, 60 sec carry
Isometric Towel Grip Hold; Bent-Over Backpack Row; Loaded Shopping Bag Carry.
“Kid, I said get a grip!” — Phil

title: MISSION 02 — PEGASUS
subtitle: FIND YOUR WINGS
paragraphs: In Disney’s Hercules, Pegasus is Hercules’ loyal flying companion, created by Zeus from clouds. He’s fast, playful, and occasionally a little too enthusiastic.
Maxi, Pegasus has heard about your marathons. He’s impressed. But apparently, running on the ground is terribly old-fashioned.
1 Goggins — 4 × (30 sec fast / 60 sec easy); 2 × 8 lunges/leg; 2 × 10 calf raises/leg
2 Goggins — 6 × (45 sec fast / 60 sec easy); 2 × 10 lunges/leg; 2 × 12 calf raises/leg
3 Goggins — 8 × (45 sec fast / 60 sec easy); 3 × 10 lunges/leg; 3 × 15 calf raises/leg
High-Knee Marching Intervals if running is unavailable; lunges and calf raises need no equipment.
NOTE — Warm up with 8–10 minutes of easy running; cool down. Leg extras are optional if fatigued.
“Fly, honey, fly! Just remember: Pegasus has wings. You have legs.” — The Muses

title: MISSION 03 — THE LERNAEAN HYDRA
subtitle: CUT ONE, FACE TWO
paragraphs: The Hydra was a terrifying, many-headed serpent. Whenever Hercules cut off one of its heads, more could grow in its place. Defeating it required persistence and a clever strategy.
Maxi, here’s the problem: Every time you think you’ve finished, the Hydra has another surprise waiting. Sounds suspiciously like signing up for another endurance race.
1 Goggins — 3 rounds: 20 sec hold, 30 sec crawl, 40 sec carry
2 Goggins — 4 rounds: 25 sec hold, 40 sec crawl, 50 sec carry
3 Goggins — 5 rounds: 30 sec hold, 45 sec crawl, 60 sec carry
Backpack Bear-Hug Carry; other movements require no equipment.
“One head down, two more to go? Honey, that’s just rude!” — The Muses

title: MISSION 04 — THE LITTLE SATYR
subtitle: PHIL’S RECOVERY ACADEMY
paragraphs: Philoctetes, better known as Phil, is Hercules’ grumpy but dedicated trainer in Disney’s Hercules. He knows that becoming a hero takes more than brute strength.
Kid, you’re not training today to impress anybody. You’re training to make sure you can still walk tomorrow. And don’t argue with your coach!
“Kid, even legends need a day off. Don’t make me say it twice!” — Phil

title: MISSION 05 — THE GOLDEN HIND
subtitle: CATCH ME IF YOU CAN
paragraphs: The Ceryneian Hind was a magnificent deer sacred to Artemis, famous for its extraordinary speed. Hercules was ordered to capture it alive.
Maxi, Artemis would like her deer back. Unfortunately, it’s fast. Really fast. And you’ve been nominated to catch it.
Progression Run — four gradually faster blocks, no all-out sprint
1 Goggins — 5 min easy + 8 min progressive + 3 min cooldown
2 Goggins — 5 min easy + 12 min progressive + 4 min cooldown
3 Goggins — 7 min easy + 16 min progressive + 5 min cooldown
NOTE — Finish comfortably rather than sprinting.
“Speed is impressive, mortal. Control is what makes it extraordinary.” — Artemis

title: MISSION 06 — THE FIVE MUSES
subtitle: REMEMBER YOUR GLORY
paragraphs: In Disney’s Hercules, the five Muses tell the story of the gods and heroes through music, humor, and plenty of attitude. Today, they’re telling yours.

Hold up, Maxilicious! You’ve crossed finish lines, conquered incredible distances, and survived challenges that most mortals wouldn’t even attempt. And you thought we weren’t keeping track? Honey, we have receipts.
What athletic achievement are you most proud of?
What was your hardest battle, and how did you overcome it?
What strength do you possess that you sometimes forget?
3 Goggins — Answer all three questions and write a personal promise
“From zero to hero? Honey, you’ve been writing your own legend for years!” — The Muses

title: MISSION 07 — THE ERYMANTHIAN BOAR
subtitle: TAME THE BEAST
paragraphs: Hercules was tasked with capturing the enormous Erymanthian Boar alive. Rather than simply overpowering it, he had to control the dangerous creature.
Maxi, there’s an angry boar charging through the mountains. Zeus says you should catch it. Phil says you should strengthen your legs first.
1 Goggins — 3 rounds: 45 sec carry, 10 lunges/leg, 8 step-ups/leg
2 Goggins — 4 rounds: 60 sec carry, 12 lunges/leg, 10 step-ups/leg
3 Goggins — 5 rounds: 75 sec carry, 14 lunges/leg, 12 step-ups/leg
Backpack Bear-Hug Carry; Stair Step-Ups on a stable step.
“Remember, kid! You’re supposed to catch the boar, not become the boar!” — Phil

title: MISSION 08 — THE UNDERWORLD FAN CLUB
subtitle: DOUBLE TROUBLE
paragraphs: Pain and Panic are Hades’ two bumbling assistants in Disney’s Hercules. Their plans usually create twice as much trouble as intended.
Maxi, Pain and Panic have invented a workout. There’s just one tiny problem. They keep doubling everything.
1 Goggins — 4 rounds: 1 → 2 → 4 → 8 reps of EACH exercise
2 Goggins — 4 rounds: 2 → 4 → 8 → 16 reps of EACH exercise
3 Goggins — 5 rounds: 2 → 4 → 8 → 16 → 32 reps of EACH exercise
NOTE — Count reps total, not per side; rest 30–90 sec as needed; scale if form deteriorates.
“We doubled the workout! Wait… was that a good idea?” — Pain & Panic

title: MISSION 09 — THE AUGEAN STABLES
subtitle: CLEAN UP YOUR MESS
paragraphs: Hercules was ordered to clean the enormous stables of King Augeas. Instead of doing everything by hand, he redirected rivers to wash away the accumulated filth.
Maxi, congratulations. You’ve been assigned the worst cleaning job in Greek mythology. Good news: No actual stable cleaning required. Bad news: Hades is disappointed.
NOTE — Prioritize relaxed walking; mobility optional.
“Sometimes the smartest hero doesn’t work harder. He finds a better way.” — The Muses

title: MISSION 10 — THE STYMPHALIAN BIRDS
subtitle: EYES ON THE TARGET
paragraphs: The Stymphalian Birds were dangerous creatures with metallic feathers. Athena helped Hercules by providing a noise-making instrument that startled them into flight.
Maxi, flying metal feathers. Terrible attitude. Absolutely no respect for personal space. Your mission? Stay balanced, move precisely, and keep your eyes on the target.
1 Goggins — 2 rounds: 6 reaches/leg, 20 sec hops, 6 target throws
2 Goggins — 3 rounds: 8 reaches/leg, 30 sec hops, 8 target throws
3 Goggins — 4 rounds: 10 reaches/leg, 40 sec hops, 10 target throws
Side-to-Side Line Hops; Rolled-Sock Target Throw.
NOTE — Target throw counts are reconstructed suggestions after replacing calf raises.
“A true warrior doesn’t simply move quickly. He knows exactly where to aim.” — Athena

title: MISSION 11 — THE THREADS OF FATE
subtitle: BEND YOUR FATE
paragraphs: In Greek mythology, the three Moirai govern the thread of human life. Clotho spins the thread. Lachesis measures its length. Atropos cuts it.
Maxi, the Fates have examined your future. Apparently, they found a few muscles that could use some stretching. Don’t worry. Atropos has promised to put the scissors away. For now.
1 Goggins — 2 rounds: 3 stretch reps/side, 20 sec hamstring/side, 30 sec squat hold
2 Goggins — 3 rounds: 4 stretch reps/side, 30 sec hamstring/side, 45 sec squat hold
3 Goggins — 4 rounds: 5 stretch reps/side, 40 sec hamstring/side, 60 sec squat hold
No equipment; use stable support for balance if needed.
“We may control the thread, mortal. But how you live your life is still your choice.” — The Fates

title: MISSION 12 — GO THE DISTANCE
subtitle: THE NEXT CHAPTER
paragraphs: In Disney’s Hercules, the hero dreams of finding the place where he truly belongs. His journey becomes about more than strength or glory. It’s about discovering who he is.

STOP THE PRESSES! The gods have an announcement. MIGHTY MAXIMILIAN IS TURNING THIRTY! Zeus has prepared the thunder. The Muses have prepared a birthday song. Hades has requested that everyone keep the noise down. And Phil? Phil says you’re officially old enough to know better.
PART ONE — THE FIRST 30 YEARS: Write 15 things you’re grateful for.
PART TWO — THE NEXT CHAPTER: Write 15 wishes, dreams, or goals for the year ahead.
PART THREE — THE FIRST STEP: Circle one wish and write one concrete action toward it.
1 Goggins — NO GOGGINS LEVELS TODAY — This day belongs to you.
NOTE — 30 Years. 30 Thoughts. One New Beginning. No workout.
“Thirty years of adventures, victories, disasters, and questionable decisions… and honey, the best chapter hasn’t even started!” — The Muses

title: MISSION 13 — THE CRETAN BULL
subtitle: *Some forces cannot be stopped. But they can be controlled.*
paragraphs: *Some forces cannot be stopped. But they can be controlled.*
The Cretan Bull was a magnificent, powerful creature that terrorized the island of Crete. Hercules was sent to capture it alive, using his strength and determination to bring the beast under control.
Mighty Maximilian, we've got a situation.
There's an angry bull running through Olympus.
Zeus wants it stopped. Phil wants to see your technique.
And Hades? He's already taking bets.
1 Goggins: 3 rounds: 10 push-ups; 15 squats; 6 sandbag lifts total
2 Goggins: 4 rounds: 15 push-ups; 20 squats; 8 lifts total
3 Goggins: 5 rounds: 20 push-ups; 25 squats; 10 lifts total
Push-Up and Bodyweight Squat → no equipment
Sandbag Ground-to-Shoulder → Backpack Deadlift (related lifting pattern, not equivalent)
NOTE  Choose a secure load; avoid twisting or jerking.
“Kid, the bull's got power. Let's see if you've got control!” — Phil the Satyr

title: MISSION 14 — THE GOLDEN APPLES
subtitle: *The prize is never handed to the hero.*
paragraphs: *The prize is never handed to the hero.*
Deep in a mysterious garden grew the Golden Apples of the Hesperides. These precious fruits were guarded by the fearsome dragon Ladon.
Hercules was tasked with retrieving the apples, a challenge that required more than simple strength.
You've been invited into the most exclusive garden in Greek mythology.
Unfortunately, the apples are guarded by a dragon.
Technique-focused pulling and core session; stop short of failure.
1 Goggins: 2 rounds: 8 rows; 20s hang; 20s hollow hold
2 Goggins: 3 rounds: 10 rows; 30s hang; 30s hollow hold
3 Goggins: 4 rounds: 12 rows; 40s hang; 40s hollow hold
Dead Hang → Isometric Towel Grip Hold
NOTE  Reduce grip work if hands/shoulders need recovery.
“Honey, if you're reaching for gold, you'd better be ready to hang on!” — The Muses

title: MISSION 15 — THE MARES OF DIOMEDES
subtitle: *Four wild horses. One very unfortunate hero.*
paragraphs: *Four wild horses. One very unfortunate hero.*
King Diomedes kept four terrifying, man-eating mares. Hercules was ordered to capture them and bring them under control.
These were no ordinary horses. They were dangerous, unpredictable, and definitely not interested in being rescued.
Maxi, meet your new training partners.
And they're all faster than your excuses.
1 Goggins: 3 rounds: 8 burpees; 10 thrusters; 30s mountain climbers
2 Goggins: 4 rounds: 10 burpees; 12 thrusters; 40s mountain climbers
3 Goggins: 5 rounds: 12 burpees; 15 thrusters; 45s mountain climbers
Burpee and Mountain Climber → no equipment
Thruster → Bodyweight Squat to Overhead Reach (lower-load substitute)
“Four man-eating horses? Honey, I'd start running!” — The Muses

title: MISSION 16 — THE THUNDERBOLT
subtitle: *Power is nothing without precision.*
paragraphs: Zeus, king of the Olympian gods, wielded the thunderbolt as a symbol of his divine power.
Lightning could strike in an instant, but true mastery required control over that power.
Maxi, Zeus has decided it's time for a little fatherly advice.
Thorough warm-up; 90–120s rest; movement quality over exhaustion.
Squat Jump → Bodyweight Squat with Calf Raise
Short Running Acceleration → High Knees in Place (different stimulus)
“A little spark, a little thunder… and preferably no property damage!” — Zeus

title: MISSION 17 — THE BELT OF HIPPOLYTA
subtitle: *Strength is earned. Respect is commanded.*
paragraphs: Hippolyta was the queen of the Amazons, a legendary nation of warrior women. Her magnificent belt was a symbol of her authority.
Hercules was sent to obtain it as one of his twelve labors.
Mighty Maximilian, the Amazons have heard about your Spartan ambitions.
But before they'll call you a warrior, they'd like to see how much you can carry.
Three carry positions; rest 60–120 seconds between rounds.
Farmer’s Carry → Loaded Shopping Bag Carry
Sandbag Bear-Hug Carry → Backpack Bear-Hug Carry
“Honey, the Amazons don't hand out respect. You carry your way to it!” — The Muses

title: MISSION 18 — THE ANCIENT TITANS
subtitle: *Four Titans. Four patterns. One warrior.*
paragraphs: Hades has unleashed four monstrous Titans upon Olympus: Earth, Wind, Fire, and Ice.
Each one moves differently. And each one brings a new kind of chaos.
Maxi, Hades has released the Titans.
Zeus is furious. Phil is screaming. And the Muses have already started writing a song about your funeral.
Your mission? Outsmart all four Titans with your footwork.
Four distinct agility-ladder patterns; one pass = one full ladder length. Accuracy first, speed second.
Agility Ladder — One Foot In Each Square (Earth)
Agility Ladder — Lateral Two Feet In Each Square (Wind)
No ladder → DIY Agility Ladder using chalk or masking tape on a flat nonslip surface
NOTE  Moderate coordination day, not maximal conditioning.
“Four Titans? Honey, even your feet are gonna need a strategy!” — The Muses
EARTH — Agility Ladder – One Foot In Each Square
WIND — Agility Ladder – Lateral Two Feet In Each Square
No ladder: mark squares with tape or chalk on a flat nonslip surface.

title: MISSION 19 — THE CATTLE OF GERYON
subtitle: *The journey is part of the trial.*
paragraphs: *The journey is part of the trial.*
For his tenth labor, Hercules was sent to retrieve the cattle of Geryon, a fearsome giant often described as having three bodies.
The herd lived far away, at the western edge of the known world. Capturing the cattle was only part of the challenge. Hercules still had to bring them all the way home.
Maxi, congratulations! You've just inherited a herd of divine cattle.
Small problem: They're on the other side of the world.
Bigger problem: Geryon wants them back.
And the biggest problem? Apparently, Olympus doesn't reimburse travel expenses.
Steady circuit: run → carry → lunges. Maintain a conversational running pace.
Farmer’s Carry → Loaded Shopping Bag Carry
If no carry load: Brisk Uphill Walk (different stimulus)
“A three-bodied giant and a herd of cows? Honey, this labor is udderly ridiculous!” — Thalia, Muse of Comedy

title: MISSION 20 — THE GATES OF HADES
subtitle: *Even heroes must know when to slow down.*
paragraphs: *Even heroes must know when to slow down.*
In Greek mythology, Charon ferried the souls of the dead across the rivers of the Underworld. The journey marked their passage from the world of the living into Hades' realm.
Today, your journey is much less permanent. Hopefully.
Maxi, welcome to the Underworld Ferry Service!
And the only thing moving quickly today is Hades' blood pressure.
Recovery only. Take complete rest instead if needed.
Gentle Mobility (Cat-Cow Stretch / Standing Hip Circles)
“No running on my boat. No shouting. And absolutely no burpees.” — Charon, Ferryman of the Underworld

title: MISSION 21 — THE LORD OF THE UNDERWORLD
subtitle: *Not every battle is fought on a battlefield.*
paragraphs: MISSION 21 — THE LORD OF THE UNDERWORLD
*Not every battle is fought on a battlefield.*
Hades rules the Underworld, a kingdom where even the greatest heroes must face the darkness.
In Disney's Hercules, Hades believes he can control everything through clever plans, manipulation, and a spectacularly bad temper.
But there's one thing he consistently underestimates: the human spirit.
You've conquered mountains, crossed finish lines, and survived challenges that would send most mortals straight back to bed.
But tell me something, Wonder Boy…
What happens when the obstacle isn't on a racecourse?
Welcome to my three favorite traps.
Life-focused reflection. Trap I: The Failed Obstacle (setbacks); Trap II: The Energy Crash (what drains/restores you); Trap III: The Unexpected Turn (changing direction).
1 Goggins: Choose one trap and answer its three questions
2 Goggins: Face all three traps; one meaningful insight from each
3 Goggins: Answer every question and write a personal promise
NOTE  No workout; answers may remain private.
“Oh, come on! You're supposed to stay trapped down here! What's with all this personal growth?!” — Hades
HADES' THREE TRAPS — LIFE REFLECTION (LATEST APPROVED VERSION)
*When life doesn't go according to plan.*
Think about a time when you failed, lost something important, or faced a setback you never saw coming.
What did that experience teach you about yourself?
What would you tell the version of yourself who was going through it?
How can you use that lesson when life challenges you again?
Not every difficult chapter comes with a finish line. Sometimes you're simply exhausted, overwhelmed, or unsure how to keep going.
What drains your energy in life, and what genuinely restores it?
How do you recognize when you need to push forward — and when you need to rest?
What could you change to protect more of your energy for the things that matter?
*When the path you imagined suddenly changes.*
Life doesn't always follow the route you've carefully planned. Sometimes the destination changes. Sometimes you do.
What is something you once wanted that no longer feels right for you?
Is there a new direction you're curious about but haven't dared to explore?
What is one small step you could take toward the life you want to build?
1 Goggins: Choose one trap and answer its three questions.
2 Goggins: Face all three traps and write down one meaningful insight from each.
3 Goggins: Face all three traps, answer every question, and write a personal promise for the year ahead.
No workout. No stopwatch. No perfect answers required. You can keep your reflections entirely private.

title: MISSION 22 — THE WILD CENTAUR
subtitle: *Speed without control is just chaos.*
paragraphs: Centaurs were creatures of Greek mythology with the upper body of a human and the lower body of a horse.
In Disney's Hercules, the aggressive centaur Nessus causes trouble for Megara, until Hercules intervenes.
Maxi, there's a centaur causing chaos.
And judging by his attitude, he has never heard of leg day.
Phil has one piece of advice:
Don't just move fast. Move smart.
Warm up. Technique-focused footwork ahead of the final physical trial.
Agility cones → shoes, bottles or chalk markers
No special equipment for shuffles or reaches
NOTE  Use marked equal distances; traditionally 5–10–5 yards.
“Two legs or four, kid — bad footwork is still bad footwork!” — Phil

title: MISSION 23 — THE GUARDIAN CERBERUS
subtitle: *Three trials stand between you and Olympus.*
paragraphs: *Three trials stand between you and Olympus.*
Cerberus, the fearsome three-headed hound, guarded the entrance to the Underworld.
For his twelfth and final labor, Hercules was ordered to capture Cerberus and bring him into the world of the living.
It was the ultimate test of courage, strength, and determination.
You've survived the lion. The Hydra. The Titans.
But now there's one final guardian.
And absolutely zero interest in letting you pass.
Three heads in order: endurance → strength → grip. Rest 60–120 seconds between rounds.
No safe bar → Isometric Towel Grip Hold or Bent-Over Backpack Row
NOTE  Optional pulling variation: approximately 6–10 controlled Inverted Rows per round. Reduce or reschedule if fatigued.
“Three heads, one hero, and not a single dog treat in sight. Honey, good luck!” — The Muses

title: MISSION 24 — A TRUE HERO
subtitle: *The greatest victory is becoming who you were meant to be.*
paragraphs: *The greatest victory is becoming who you were meant to be.*
Hercules spent years proving his strength, facing monsters, completing impossible labors, and searching for his place among the gods.
But in Disney's Hercules, his greatest discovery was that being a true hero was never simply about power or fame.
It was about the strength of his heart.
One very dramatic journey through Olympus.
The Muses have sung. Phil has shouted. Zeus has thrown lightning bolts.
And Hades has filed approximately seventeen complaints.
Final reflection: (I) one strength discovered; (II) one lesson to carry forward; (III) complete “In the year ahead, I promise myself that I will…”
1 Goggins: No Goggins levels — finale exception
3 Goggins: Write and keep your personal oath
NOTE  Final day is intentionally non-physical.
“A true hero isn't measured by the size of his strength, but by the strength of his heart.” — Zeus, Disney’s Hercules
Today, there are no burpees. No carries. No running.
What is one strength you discovered or rediscovered during these 24 days?
What is one lesson you want to carry into your next year of training and life?
Complete this sentence: “In the year ahead, I promise myself that I will…”
Write it down. Keep it somewhere you can return to when the next challenge begins.
MAXIMILIAN — THE LEGEND NOBODY SAW COMING.
THE GODS SET THE TRIAL. YOU CHOSE THE BATTLE. YOU BECAME THE WARRIOR.
THE END… OR JUST THE BEGINNING?
